questions.stem: An acquirer starts putting a device ID into field 63 of its authorization requests, for issuers' fraud checks. The network's rules for that link have no place for it. What reaches an issuer that receives one of these purchases?

options.text: The purchase without the device ID, since the network passes on only what the next link's specification defines
options.says: each hop is its own link and the message is rebuilt for it, so a field the network's specification does not carry stops there

options.text: The purchase without the device ID, since the acquirer's own link drops field 63 before the request leaves
options.says: the acquirer chose to send it on its link; it is the next hop, the network, that does not carry it

options.text: The purchase with the device ID, since the network forwards the acquirer's request as it arrived
options.says: the network rebuilds the message for the issuer's link; it is not a pipe

options.text: The purchase with the device ID, since a private field travels from end to end untouched
options.says: a private field means what each link's specification says, and a field the next link does not define does not get across

origin.section: 7.1. A Payment Crosses Four Parties, and Each Hop Is a Link of Its Own

questions.stem: A café's terminal gets its 0100s approved all week, but a configuration error keeps its batch from ever reaching the acquirer. Three weeks later, where do those purchases stand?

options.text: The cardholders were never charged and the café was never paid, since the holds lapsed with nothing to post
options.says: an approval only holds the money; without a clearing record nothing posts, and the issuer drops the hold after some days

options.text: The cardholders were never charged but the café was paid, since the network settles every approved authorization
options.says: settlement pays what was cleared; an authorization alone moves no money

options.text: The cardholders were charged and the café was paid, since each approval moved the money when it was given
options.says: an approved 0100 places a hold; the money moves with the clearing record

options.text: The cardholders were charged but the café is still owed, since the issuer posted each hold when it lapsed
options.says: a lapsed hold is released, not posted; nothing posts without a clearing record

origin.section: 7.2. An Approval Holds the Money in the Dual-Message Flow and Moves It in the Single-Message Flow

questions.stem: On one settlement day a bank's merchants sell 41,200.00 to other banks' cardholders, and the bank's own cardholders spend 38,950.00 at other banks' merchants. Leaving fees aside, what happens to the bank's settlement account that day?

options.text: It receives 2,250.00 in one transfer, since the network sets what the bank is owed against what it owes
options.says: settlement moves one net amount per institution: 41,200.00 owed to it less 38,950.00 it owes

options.text: It receives 41,200.00 and pays 38,950.00, since sales and purchases are settled as two separate sums
options.says: the network nets each member's position into one amount

options.text: It moves money once per purchase, since each cleared purchase is paid between the two banks as it clears
options.says: no single purchase appears in a transfer of its own; the day's positions are netted

options.text: It moves nothing at all, since the 05xx exchange settles the totals once both ends agree on them
options.says: 05xx messages let the two ends agree on totals and move no money themselves

origin.section: 7.3. Settlement Moves One Net Amount per Institution, Days After the Purchases

questions.stem: A cardholder reports an 89.00 charge for goods that never arrived. The purchase cleared nine days ago, and the merchant does not answer. What brings the 89.00 back?

options.text: A chargeback from the issuer, in clearing, since the purchase is past the point a reversal can reach
options.says: a cleared purchase is undone by a refund from the merchant or a chargeback from the issuer, through the network's dispute process

options.text: A reversal from the issuer, on the online link, since field 90 can still name the purchase
options.says: a reversal works only within the network's window, typically before clearing, and it is the acquirer's message

options.text: A reversal from the acquirer, on the online link, since only the merchant's side may undo a purchase
options.says: nine days after clearing a reversal is past the window; the issuer can start a chargeback

options.text: A chargeback from the acquirer, in clearing, since the merchant's bank answers for its merchant
options.says: the chargeback is the issuer's step; the acquirer's answer to it is the representment

origin.section: 7.5. What Undoes a Transaction Depends on How Far It Has Gone
